defects.detail: 'The king shall not compel the return ... by the act of God, water, or by thieves' — source 'राज्ञा दैवेनोदकादिना तस्करैर्वा' makes the king a cause of loss (ref: removed by the king, or God, or thieves)
'placing an item in the hands of the members of a household in the absence of the master' drops 'गृहस्वामिनेऽदर्शयित्वा' (without showing it to him)
root 67 'borrowed items, sub-deposits, trusts, and sealed deposits' drops 'आदिषु' (and so forth), which the commentary then explains
'the remainder of a debt' for 'वृद्धिशेषं' (balance of interest)
'The king shall not make the holder pay ... by an act of God, such as fire or water, or by thieves' — source 'राज्ञा दैवेनोदकादिना तस्करैर्वा' lists the king among the causes of loss

reason: Both misread राज्ञा in the opening gloss as the one who compels rather than a cause of loss (the Narada verse 'दैवराजकृते' is right in both); otherwise both follow root 66b-67 and the Mitakshara closely. T1 additionally drops अदर्शयित्वा, the आदि of the root verse, and renders वृद्धिशेषं as remainder of a debt. Reference covers root verses only.

Both make Cheng the one who thrashes Zhong and Xin and both read 三弟 as 'third brother'. Source OCR is garbled at 孝孝 and 皆謂空愧首. Reference starts before the page.
